01.establishes: The exact byte stream the MCU is allowed to see. Everything later is compared against these bytes.
01.inspect: The canonical 64x64 GRAY8 source image and its flash layout.
01.look: Dimensions 64x64, frame id, the raw pixel hash; pixel (x,y) lives at flash address 20 + y*64 + x.
01.title: Input image

02.establishes: The image arrived through the simulated SPI flash into SRAM (no testbench preload), byte for byte.
02.inspect: The input SRAM buffer filling through the SPI path.
02.look: SPI chip-select bursts per row read; committed SRAM writes accumulating; orange cells are bytes not yet written at that point in the reconstruction.
02.title: Load overview

03.establishes: Waveform bytes and image pixels are the same bytes, at the stated addresses.
03.inspect: One complete SPI read (row 32) decoded byte by byte.
03.look: MOSI command 0x03 and address 0x000814, MISO bytes matching the row's pixels, then the SRAM writes landing at the input buffer + 2048.
03.title: Load detail

04.artifact: stage04_pixel.png + stage06_writeback.vcd (gradient writes precede the combine of stripe 8)
04.establishes: The firmware computes exactly the specified operator, verified against the independent OpenCV reference.
04.inspect: The Sobel arithmetic for pixel (32,32) and its committed gradient writes.
04.look: The 3x3 neighborhood, signed Gx and Gy from the Section 2.2 formulas, the clamp; then the actual int16 writes in the Gx/Gy buffers with their cycles.
04.title: Algorithm

05.establishes: Dependencies were enforced by blocking queues, not timing luck: no Combine stripe precedes both of its gradient publications.
05.inspect: Why GradientX and GradientY are independent, why Combine waits, and the observed interleaving.
05.look: Retired-PC classification bands (workers share one body function; kernel code is labeled shared), trap events, and the GX/GY publication traces strictly preceding each Combine trace.
05.title: RTOS scheduling

06.establishes: The canonical generated image is the SRAM content itself, not a host-side rendering.
06.inspect: The output framebuffer being written into SRAM, progressively.
06.look: Accepted byte writes with strobes and values; the write of pixel (32,32) at offset 2080. In the fault run this stage pauses at the injection: same write, bit 7 flipped, injection pulse recorded.
06.title: Memory writeback

07.establishes: What left the MCU is what was in SRAM, with packet integrity proven by the digest.
07.inspect: The stored framebuffer read back and exported as one packet.
07.look: One readable byte excerpt on the TX pin correlated with framebuffer offsets; the packet is header + 4096 pixels + SHA-256, then 50,000 quiet cycles with no extra byte.
07.title: UART recovery

08.artifact: stage08_compare.png (+ stage08_crop.png when a mismatch exists) + results.json
08.establishes: Baseline: zero mismatches across every observation. Fault run: the unchanged checker rejects exactly the injected pixel.
08.inspect: MCU image vs the independent OpenCV reference, and the checker verdicts.
08.look: Side-by-side images and the difference map; compared byte count, mismatch count, and the per-observation checker results. In the fault run the single wrong pixel is highlighted with its crop.
08.title: Reference comparison
